messages.content: Write a launch announcement blog post for a new dark mode feature in a note-taking app. Around 250 words.

output:
Passes clean. Here's the post (about 230 words):

## Dark mode is here

We shipped dark mode this week. Open Settings, tap Appearance, and pick Dark, Light, or Match System. The switch is instant, and every note, folder, and editor screen follows the same palette.

We built this because it was the most requested feature in our support inbox for over a year. Late-night writers kept telling us the same thing: a bright white editor at midnight hurts. So we rebuilt the color system from scratch instead of just inverting the existing one, which meant checking contrast on every element by hand.

A few details we cared about. Syntax highlighting in code blocks got new colors tuned for a dark background, not just dimmed versions of the light set. Headers, tags, and links keep enough contrast to stay readable. And if you use Match System, the app switches automatically at sunset or whenever your OS theme changes, no restart needed.

This took three designers and two engineers about six weeks, mostly spent on edge cases: shared note previews, exported PDFs, the widget on your home screen. All of it now respects your theme choice.

Dark mode rolls out today on iOS, Android, and web. If you're on an older app version, update from your app store and it'll be waiting in Settings.

We read every piece of feedback that comes through the app, so if something looks off in dark mode, tell us and we'll fix it.
